yarn-troppo.meaning: All the technical content survives (install commands, Python 3.10+, the standalone executables, the AST check, `--fast`). It adds claims and asides: "No more scrolling through a mile of whitespace changes.", "so you're in good company", "Bliss.", "Better safe than sorry." "full stop" adds emphasis the original lacks. These mostly hang off the original.
yarn-troppo.sense: The terms fit: "does not budge" for uncompromising, "fiddly little bits" for minutiae, "easy as", "won't play ball", "No Python on the box? No worries.", "down the track".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: There's real Aussie idiom ("easy as", "No worries", "won't play ball", "get cracking"), but the opener and tags are stock: "So get this.", "Not an inch.", "Bliss.", "Which is the whole point, really."
yarn-troppo.register: Much heavier than level 2 for a README: it is a chatty performance with added openers and tags ("So get this.", "One last thing.", "and yeah, it does slow processing down a bit"). There's no swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: The original is crisp and confident; A turns it into salesy banter ("Bliss.", "you're in good company"), though the documentation still reads as helpful.
yarn-troppo.flow: Readable, but choppy with fragment tags: "and it does not budge. Not an inch.", "Bliss.", "Better safe than sorry."
yarn-troppo.variety: The slang and openers vary ("easy as", "No worries", "play ball", "get cracking", "squiz", "heaps"), though the short-tag tic recurs.
yarn-troppo.essence: It is still the Black README, structure intact, but its terse confidence becomes chatter.

engine.meaning: Identical to the original apart from "Any colour you like."
engine.sense: There are no Aussie terms to misfire; "colour" is right.
engine.authenticity: There's no Aussie at all; it is the original's formal README voice ("you agree to cede control over minutiae of hand-formatting").
engine.register: Untranslated. Only the spelling "colour" changes, far under level 2.
engine.tone: The original tone, unchanged: "_Black_ is the uncompromising Python code formatter."
engine.variety: There is no slang, so nothing to vary or repeat.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point is kept and nothing is invented; "which does slow processing down a bit" softens "slows down processing" only slightly.
yarn-dinkum.sense: The terms fit: "won't budge" for uncompromising, "fiddly bits", "get cracking", "Heaps of projects", "down the track", "have a squiz", "grab".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural, matter-of-fact Aussie technical writing: "don't go expecting big formatting changes down the track", "For the full rundown, have a squiz at".
yarn-dinkum.register: A light, consistent touch at level 2, with a sprinkling of idiom and a casual voice and no tags. There's no swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: It keeps the confident, direct README voice: "_Black_ is the Python code formatter that won't budge."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads smoothly: "After a while you stop even noticing the formatting, and you can get on with the content instead."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "won't budge", "fiddly bits", "get cracking", "Heaps", "down the track", "squiz", "rundown".

unharnessed.meaning: Faithful throughout; "effectively the same as" for "effectively equivalent to" is fine.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly apt ("fiddly bits", "get cracking", "down the track", "have a squiz"), but "no-nonsense" softens uncompromising: no-nonsense is plain and practical, not unbending.
unharnessed.authenticity: The swaps are natural: "Have a squiz at the", "grab one of the", "down the track".
unharnessed.register: A light touch at about level 2, a shade lighter than C. There's no swearing.
unharnessed.tone: It keeps the README voice intact.
unharnessed.flow: Smooth throughout: "After a while the formatting stops being something you notice".
unharnessed.variety: Varied, with each term used once: "no-nonsense", "fiddly bits", "squiz", "get cracking", "down the track".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the original. "no-nonsense" slightly dulls the defining "uncompromising".

yarn-deadset.meaning: Faithful throughout; nothing lost or added.
yarn-deadset.sense: Mostly apt ("nitty-gritty" for minutiae, "get cracking", "down the track", "have a squiz", "heaps of projects"); "no-nonsense" softens uncompromising.
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural, though "nitty-gritty" is general English rather than Australian; "heaps of projects" and "have a squiz" are local.
yarn-deadset.register: A light touch, slightly under level 2; much of the text is the original wording ("_Black_ can be installed by running", "Watch the").
yarn-deadset.tone: It keeps the README tone intact.
yarn-deadset.variety: There are few terms, each used once: "nitty-gritty", "get cracking", "heaps", "squiz", "down the track".
yarn-deadset.essence: It is the original, lightly accented.
